item.title: Ballinlough beef farmer elected as Roscommon IFA chairman
item.description: A west Roscommon beef farmer has been elected as the chairman of Roscommon IFA. Ballinlough's Seán Finan was chosen to succeed Pat Leonard last night. item.title: Paddy Berrigan
item.description: Paddy Berrigan Clonark, Athlone Paddy Berrigan passed away on Thursday, February 27th, peacefully in the tender, care of the staff of St. Brendan Nursing Home, Ballinasloe. Predeceased by his parents; Thomas and Delia, and brothers; Michael, Tommy and Willie. Deeply regretted by his cousin Adrian Ward, his wife Siobhan and their family David, Leanne and Amy, relatives, neighbours and his many close friends, whose friendship meant so much to him over the years. item.title: Cian McPhillips to miss World indoor championship
item.description: Cian McPhillips has decided to miss next month’s World indoor championships in Torun, Poland. The Longford athlete had intended to race at the championships and was considered as a medal contender. However, having with drawn from the Milrose Games 800m due to a dental issue, McPhillips has now decided to focus on his outdoor season. item.title: Celebrations continue in Castlerea after All-Ireland Basketball title
item.description: Celebrations are continuing in West Roscommon today after the Castlerea Community School's Under-19 basketball team won the All-Ireland B League title. They beat Kildare Town Community School by 50 points to 45 yesterday. Local man Danny Burke says there's a great tradition of Basketball in Castlerea: Advertisement

item.title: Protest over SNA allocations to take place in Longford tomorrow
item.description: A protest over SNA allocations is set to take place in Longford Town tomorrow afternoon. The protest is going ahead at the Market Square despite the Government doing a U-turn on planned cuts. Similar protests took place earlier this week in Castlerea and Roscommon Town. James Donnelly is one of the organisers of the Longford Town protest. He says there's still concerns that cuts may happen in the future: Advertisement

item.title: Over 50 people registered as homeless in the region last month
item.description: 55 people registered as homeless in the Shannonside region last month. The Department of Housing says there were 21 in Longford, 18 in Roscommon and 16 in Leitrim. Nationally, 17,112 people were accessing emergency accommodation in January. It's the first time the number of people experiencing homelessness has surpassed 17,000. Advertisement

item.title: Final chapter of 'One Mystery, One Town' written in Edgeworthstown today
item.description: The final chapter of One Mystery, One Town was written this morning at Edgeworthstown Library. Students and artists gathered to celebrate the project's conclusion. The initiative brought young readers together to explore storytelling, creativity and community through a shared mystery novel- The Case of the Vanishing Painting. Author, Brian Gallagher was heartened by the response of the students: Advertisement

item.title: Local Enterprise Week set to kick off on Monday
item.description: Small and medium businesses in Leitrim can avail of a number of free online and in person workshops next week. It's part of Local Enterprise Week which starts next Monday and runs until Friday afternoon. Hundreds of online and in person events are taking place at venues across the country as part of the initiative. Head of Enterprise in Letirim, Joe Lowe, highlights some of the events on offer: Advertisement

item.title: Eileen Gillen (nee Cosgrove)
item.description: Eileen Gillen (nee Cosgrove) Corlea, Killoe, Longford and formerly of Bawn. Thursday, 26th February, peacefully in her 93rd year, after a short illness. Surrounded by her loving family in the care of the staff of Mullingar Regional Hospital Eileen Gillen (nee Cosgrove), predeceased by her husband Pat, parents; Patrick and Ellen, brothers; Eugene and Patrick, sisters; Margaret and Bridget. Eileen will be sadly missed and forever remembered with love by her family, daughters; Bridget and Patricia

item.title: Drogheda United to pay Dundalk pitch repairs
item.description: Drogheda United have confirmed they will pay the full cost of repairing Dundalk’s pitch after last week’s Louth derby. The League of Ireland had imposed a €15,000 fine on the club after last Friday’s game; where Drogheda fans threw flares onto the Oriel Park pitch. The incident was heavily condemned by minister for sport Patrick O’Donovan who was in attendance.
